hotspot.p: Giveback powers the giving here: a micro-economy of giving, where business activity, purchases and community participation automatically become giving, in any form, verified on chain. The hall follows capital from a corporate bank account to verified giving, one station at a time, beside the ledger wall. Take the wide stair on the north side up to the terrace, where Ana Ruiz, the ledger guide, explains how giving moves through Genesis.

will.name: Ana Ruiz
greet: The Ring looks best from up here.

talk.t: Welcome to the terrace. I'm Ana Ruiz, the ledger guide here at GBANK. I can walk you through how giving moves, from a purchase to a verified cause. Where would you like to start?

Downstairs in the GBANK hall you can follow it end to end. Funds start in a corporate bank account, cross onto the blockchain through the Altitude bridge, and sit in a Squads multisig treasury, where several signers must approve every movement. The Giveback protocol then routes each transaction and records it on chain, and giving reaches nonprofits and causes vetted in house by Giveback's own compliance team.

On chain means the record lives on a public blockchain, here Solana, where anyone can check it and no one can quietly change it. The ledger wall downstairs shows what that stream looks like: signatures, routes and confirmations.
$GBACK is a utility token: access, memberships and the rails that make giving automatic. It is not an investment, and Giveback Ventures is its largest holder, not its issuer.
Giveback's own compliance team vets every nonprofit and community cause in house before any giving reaches it. The last station of the capital flow downstairs shows where that check happens.
My pleasure. Enjoy the terrace on your way out; the view down to the Ring is the best in The Expanse. $GBACK is a utility for giving, never an investment.
